gloss: to crawl into; to creep into

definitions.gloss: to crawl into; to creep into; to slip into
definitions.explanation: To enter a place by crawling, creeping, or sneaking in. Can describe physically crawling into a space or figuratively sneaking into somewhere.

examples.japanese: {布団|ふとん}に{這|は}い{込|こ}む。
{猫|ねこ}がベッドの{下|した}に{這|は}い{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: The cat crawled under the bed.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちが{狭|せま}いトンネルに{這|は}い{込|こ}んで{遊|あそ}んでいた。
examples.english: The children were playing by crawling into a narrow tunnel.

examples.japanese: {疲|つか}れて{帰|かえ}ってきて、そのまま{布団|ふとん}に{這|は}い{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: I came home exhausted and crawled straight into the futon.

notes:
A compound verb formed from {這|は}う (to crawl) and {込|こ}む (to go into). Describes entering somewhere by crawling or on all fours. The most common use is {布団|ふとん}に{這|は}い{込|こ}む, conveying the image of tiredly or eagerly getting into bed.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {布団|ふとん}に{這|は}い{込|こ}む: to crawl into the futon
- ベッドに{這|は}い{込|こ}む: to crawl into bed
- {隙間|すきま}に{這|は}い{込|こ}む: to crawl into a gap

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {潜|もぐ}り{込|こ}む: to slip into, to sneak in — emphasizes hiding or getting under something
- {忍|しの}び{込|こ}む: to sneak in — emphasizes stealth, often with intent to trespass
- {入|はい}り{込|こ}む: to go into, to enter deeply — more general entering, not necessarily crawling

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive. Takes the particle に to mark the destination.
